meta.title: Deploy an Open Model with vLLM
meta.thesis: Deploy an Open Model with vLLM is practical when learners can apply it to this concrete case: A team deploys an open model for ticket summaries and must hit latency and cost limits. By the end, they should be able to build or review vLLM deployment checklist with model, batching, and rollback settings, measure p95 latency under the release target, and catch the failure where throughput looks fine in a demo but collapses under concurrent users.

modules.title: Choose the open model and serving target
modules.sub: Start with model, traffic shape, and GPU budget.
modules.summary: A vLLM deployment begins with model choice, context budget, and traffic assumptions.
objectives: Separate production endpoint from local demo.

blocks.title: The product constraint is GPU memory under load

spans.text: Problem anchor: a support-agent team wants to serve an open instruction model for many concurrent users. Hosted APIs are too costly for expected volume, and data locality matters. vLLM is a fit because it focuses on high-throughput online serving, continuous batching, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, and efficient KV-cache management.

blocks.analogy: vLLM is an airport scheduler for token generation: it keeps many flights moving through limited gates.

spans.text: Model: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Traffic: 20 concurrent chats, p95 prompt 2k tokens, p95 output 400 tokens. Hardware: two GPUs. Release target: OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint with streaming, health checks, metrics, and load test before production.

options.text: A one-off laptop demo with no concurrency.
High-throughput self-hosted serving where GPU memory, batching, and KV cache matter.

modules.title: Budget weights, context, and KV cache before launch
modules.sub: Weights, context length, batch size, and cache all compete for accelerator memory.
modules.summary: PagedAttention reduces waste but does not remove memory limits.
objectives: Name why prefix caching helps only some workloads.

blocks.title: PagedAttention manages memory; it does not make memory infinite

spans.text: vLLM is known for PagedAttention, which manages key/value cache in blocks to reduce waste. The practical constraint remains: model weights, active prompt tokens, generated tokens, batch size, and context length compete for GPU memory. Long context serving leaves less room for concurrent users.

cells.text: long context and many active tokens
shorter context, batching limits, more GPUs
prefix caching when prefixes match exactly

modules.title: Expose an OpenAI-compatible endpoint
modules.sub: Compatibility helps, but integration tests still matter.
modules.summary: Apps can often use existing OpenAI clients against vLLM, with caveat tests.
objectives: Call it with an OpenAI-style client.
Test unsupported parameters and chat templates.

blocks.title: Compatibility is an integration surface, not a guarantee

spans.text: vLLM exposes OpenAI-compatible serving endpoints, which lets many apps point an OpenAI client at a self-hosted base URL. But provider-specific parameters, tool behavior, chat templates, and streaming details still need tests. Chat-tuned models especially need correct templates.

items.text: List models endpoint returns the expected model name.
Chat completion works with the app message format.
Streaming chunks parse in the UI.
Tool-call or structured-output behavior is tested before release.

modules.title: Run the server and smoke-test streaming
modules.sub: The first production slice proves launch, request, stream, and metrics.
modules.summary: A minimal server command plus client call catches deployment mistakes early.

blocks.title: vLLM launch and OpenAI-compatible smoke test
blocks.code:
vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct   --host 0.0.0.0   --port 8000   --tensor-parallel-size 2   --enable-prefix-caching

python - <<'PY'
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="local")
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain KV cache in two sentences."}],
    stream=False,
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content[:200])
PY

spans.text: This is the thin slice: server starts, the model name matches, the client can call it, and the app can parse the response. Load and safety tests come after this smoke test passes.

predictThenReveal.prompt: What likely happens if the client uses a model name different from the served model ID?
predictThenReveal.answer: The request can fail with an unknown model or routing error. The app should assert the served model list before release.

spans.text: Checklist: model ID and license reviewed; tensor or pipeline parallel settings match hardware; chat template works; streaming parsed; health and metrics exposed; prefix caching only assumed for exact shared prefixes; and dev-only endpoints are not public.

modules.title: Load-test, monitor, and protect the endpoint
modules.sub: Throughput is useless without reliability, budgets, and safe exposure.
modules.summary: A vLLM endpoint needs load tests, metrics, routing policy, and operational safeguards.
objectives: Know when to put a gateway in front.

blocks.title: The server is not the whole serving system

spans.text: Production checks include p50/p95 latency, tokens per second, time to first token, GPU memory, active requests, queueing, error rate, cost per tenant, and quality evals. Put a gateway in front when you need tenant keys, budgets, routing, fallback to hosted models, or one logical model name across replicas.

blocks.ruleOfThumb: Ship vLLM when load tests, integration tests, metrics, auth, and rollback are all in place.
blocks.useWhen: Use it for self-hosted high-throughput open-model serving where GPU utilization matters.
blocks.avoidWhen: Avoid exposing raw dynamic endpoints, cache reset tools, or unauthenticated model APIs in production.

blocks.title: Hardening gate
blocks.prompt: What should pass before a vLLM endpoint serves users?

options.text: Load tests, integration tests, monitoring, auth/routing policy, and quality checks.

blocks.explanation: Production serving needs operations around the model runtime.

prototype.label: Prototype
prototype.laymanDefinition: A narrow runnable slice that proves one infrastructure behavior.
prototype.technicalNote: A good prototype includes setup, smoke test, failure mode, and migration boundary.

retriever.label: Retriever
retriever.laymanDefinition: A component that fetches context or records for a request.
retriever.technicalNote: Serving lessons track retrievers because retrieval shape affects latency, cost, and quality.

validator.label: Validator
validator.laymanDefinition: A check that enforces output, request, or deployment contracts.
validator.technicalNote: Validators protect schemas, health checks, citations, policy gates, and readiness criteria.

trace.label: Trace
trace.laymanDefinition: A structured record of one request or job through serving components.
trace.technicalNote: Traces reveal queue time, model call latency, token counts, errors, and release metadata.

deployment.label: Deployment
deployment.laymanDefinition: A versioned runtime configuration exposed to users or systems.
deployment.technicalNote: A deployment includes model, serving flags, hardware, API contract, monitoring, rollback, and ownership.

acceptance_test.label: Acceptance test
acceptance_test.laymanDefinition: A test that proves the build meets its release contract.
acceptance_test.technicalNote: Acceptance tests should cover smoke behavior, failure modes, metrics, and rollback expectations.
